headline: David Bailey opens the season on top — but only one point separates the top four.
summary: David Bailey’s Dave's Dream Team takes the first BFL lead with 67 points, edging Will Finney by a single point after both deployed Bench Boost. With olly barnes on 65 and Jamie Mitchell on 64, the title race is already packed tighter than a 25-manager league has any right to be in GW1.
report:
GW1 has delivered immediate title-race chaos: David Bailey leads the Biddenham Fantasy League on 67 points, but Will Finney’s 0v3rf1tt3d.h5 is just one point back on 66. There is another one-point gap to olly barnes and Grasshoppers on 65, followed by Jamie Mitchell’s wataru doing? on 64 and amy warden’s Palmer Violets on 63. No movement yet, naturally, but with 37 gameweeks remaining, this is an absurdly tight opening five.

David Bailey is the first Manager of the Week and the early pace-setter, posting 67 points with no hits. The decisive flair came from a Bench Boost and a 13-point differential in Stach, while White added 11 points as one of only two owners. It was not entirely painless: David handed the captaincy to Haaland for 2 points, making him the week’s captaincy howler despite taking top spot.

Will Finney also Bench Boosted and finished on 66, one point short of the summit. olly barnes followed the same chip route for 65, with White’s 11 points and a solitary-owned 11 from Ødegaard helping Grasshoppers stay right on the leaders’ heels. Jamie Mitchell’s Bench Boost produced 64, meaning all four early front-runners have already spent the same chip — with 21 Bench Boosts now remaining across the league.

Haaland was the overwhelmingly popular captain, selected by 18 managers, and his 2 points left plenty of armbands looking rather underwhelming. Abi Speight found the captaincy sweet spot instead, backing Havertz for 6 points with the multiplier of 2. Elsewhere, João Pedro’s 11 points rewarded 17 owners, while Calafiori delivered 9 for 13 managers; the more heavily owned B.Fernandes, Kinsky, Mbeumo and Semenyo all returned 2, and Calvert-Lewin managed 1.

The differential board was properly lively. Phil Johnson alone owned M.Sangaré and collected 14 points, the best of the listed differentials. Mark Horton’s Kayode returned 13, while Palmer also scored 13 for Dan Birkinshaw and amy warden. David’s Stach and olly’s Ødegaard were the premium one-owner calls among the chasing pack.

At the other end, Chris Beeden’s ParkToon26 takes the opening wooden spoon with 30 points. Callum Bowness is level on that 30-point last-three figure as the coldest early form entry, while James Marshall will be staring at 20 bench points and wondering what might have been. David Bailey, meanwhile, owns the season record already: 67 points in GW1, and a one-point lead that looks anything but comfortable.
